The fact that g1g3 is 10% while g2 is 0% suggests that G2 has some residual function even without G1 and G3? Or there is some other minor pathway. But it's a difference. In the second model (G1, G3 upstream TFs), g2 = 0% (effector gone), g1g3 = 10% (effector G2 still has some basal expression even without TFs, or other TFs contribute). That difference (10% vs 0%) is easier to explain if G2 is the downstream effector: its expression is not completely abolished in g1g3 because of basal transcription or other regulators. If G2 is an upstream TF, its targets G1 and G3 are the effectors; if they are completely deleted, the TF can't magically create resistance, so it should be 0%. So the 10% suggests that G1 and G3 are regulators, and G2 is the effector that has some basal level. Thus G1 and G3 are likely the TFs (or at least one of them). The problem says "at least one of these genes is a transcription factor acting upstream of (an)other gene(s)". This fits G1 and/or G3 acting upstream of G2.
